SEARCH
Package org.aristonis.diwan.database

Interface Connection

All Known Subinterfaces:
TransactionScope
public interface Connection
Sends SQL to one database and manages transactions on it.

Every SQL method comes in two forms: one taking varargs bindings and one taking a List<?>. Binding values are checked before any session is opened; the accepted types are null, Boolean, Byte, Short, Integer, Long, Float, Double, BigDecimal, BigInteger, String, byte[], LocalDate, LocalTime, LocalDateTime, OffsetDateTime, OffsetTime and Instant.

A connection obtained from builder() holds no session between calls and is safe to share between threads. A connection handed to a TransactionCallback or PretendCallback, and a TransactionScope, belong to the thread that received them.

API Note:
This interface is not meant to be implemented outside this library. Methods added in later versions arrive as default methods, so code that calls it keeps compiling.

    • unprepared

      boolean unprepared(String sql)
      Runs SQL without preparing it or binding parameters.

      On SQLite a script of several statements runs whole, one statement after another. Outside a transaction each statement commits on its own, so a failure partway leaves the earlier ones applied; run the script in a transaction when it must be all or nothing.

      Parameters:
      sql - the SQL to run, never null
      Returns:
      true once the SQL ran
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if sql is null
      QueryException - if the database refuses the SQL or no session can be opened
      API Note:
      This runs raw SQL exactly as given: nothing is bound, quoted or escaped. Never pass untrusted text, and never build sql from user input; use a prepared method with bindings instead.

    • cursor

      default QueryCursor<Map<String,Object>> cursor(String sql, Object... bindings)
      Runs a read and streams its rows through a QueryCursor, one row at a time.

      The cursor must be closed, best with try-with-resources; it also closes itself when its last row is read. On the root connection it holds a session of its own until then, so a cursor that is neither read to the end nor closed keeps a pooled connection out of the pool. Inside a transaction, a session callback or a transaction scope, it borrows that session: until it is closed, every other statement, cursor, savepoint, commit or rollback on that session is refused, and ending the transaction level or scope that opened it closes it first.

      Rows are unmodifiable, with columns in select order. A failure while reading closes the cursor and is thrown as a QueryException. The cursor belongs to the calling thread.

      The cursor holds its session until it is closed, so a long loop over it leaves a PostgreSQL connection idle in transaction. Writing through the same database inside the loop needs a second connection, and a pool of one deadlocks. For a slow loop or one that writes, read in pages instead, as lazy() on the query builder does.

      Parameters:
      sql - the read to run, never null
      bindings - the positional binding values, as for select(String, Object...)
      Returns:
      the open cursor, never null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if sql is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if bindings is a null array or holds a value of an unsupported type
      IllegalStateException - if a cursor is already open on the borrowed session, or on the root connection when this thread is inside a transaction it opened (strict mode)
      UnsupportedOperationException - in pretend mode, or if the driver cannot stream
      QueryException - if the database refuses the read or no session can be opened
      Implementation Requirements:
      The default throws UnsupportedOperationException; every connection of this library overrides it.

    • transaction

      <T> T transaction(TransactionCallback<T> callback)
      Runs a callback inside a transaction and returns its result.

      On the root connection this starts a real transaction, or a savepoint when the session is already inside a transaction Diwan Database does not own, commits when the callback returns and rolls back when it throws. Inside a transaction it nests through a savepoint.

      Type Parameters:
      T - the type of the result
      Parameters:
      callback - the work to run, never null
      Returns:
      the result of the callback, may be null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if callback is null
      QueryException - if the database refuses to start, commit or roll back the transaction
      RuntimeException - any failure of the callback, rethrown after the rollback

    • transaction

      default <T> T transaction(TransactionCallback<T> callback, int attempts)
      Runs a callback inside a transaction, retrying the whole transaction after a concurrency failure.

      The callback runs again from the start on each attempt, including any outside effect it has, such as an HTTP call or a sent message. Only the outermost transaction Diwan Database owns retries; a nested call rethrows a concurrency failure at once.

      Type Parameters:
      T - the type of the result
      Parameters:
      callback - the work to run, never null
      attempts - the most times to run the callback, at least 1
      Returns:
      the result of the successful attempt, may be null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if callback is null
      IllegalArgumentException - if attempts is below 1
      QueryException - if the database refuses to start, commit or roll back the transaction
      RuntimeException - the failure of the last attempt, rethrown after the rollback

    • transaction

      <T> T transaction(TransactionCallback<T> callback, TransactionOptions options)
      Runs a callback inside a transaction with the given options, retrying the whole transaction after a concurrency failure when the options allow more than one attempt.

      A lock wait applies to the outermost transaction only. A transaction that waits longer for a lock than the limit fails with a QueryException of kind DriverFailureKind.CONCURRENCY, which the attempts of the options retry; each attempt applies the wait again. The wait is taken back when the transaction ends; a failure to take it back is added as suppressed to the failure of the work, or thrown when the work succeeded. Inside an external transaction Diwan Database does not own, the wait is not applied.

      Type Parameters:
      T - the type of the result
      Parameters:
      callback - the work to run, never null
      options - the lock wait and attempts, never null
      Returns:
      the result of the successful attempt, may be null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if callback or options is null
      IllegalStateException - if called inside a transaction with a lock wait; no SQL is sent
      UnsupportedOperationException - if the driver cannot limit the wait for a lock
      QueryException - if the database refuses to start, commit or roll back the transaction
      RuntimeException - the failure of the last attempt, rethrown after the rollback

    • beginJoinedTransaction

      @Internal default TransactionScope beginJoinedTransaction()
      Starts a transaction that the calling thread's other calls on this connection join; a testing hook, for rolling back everything a test did.

      It opens a transaction like beginTransaction(): TransactionScope.commit() commits it, and TransactionScope.close() without a commit rolls it back. While it is open, every call the opening thread makes on this connection runs on the scope's transaction, instead of being refused by strict transactions or borrowing a session of its own. A transaction(TransactionCallback) from that thread becomes a savepoint inside the joined transaction, so a lockWait option fails with IllegalStateException and attempts are ignored, as for any nested transaction; beginTransaction() from that thread opens a nested scope the same way, and fails while an inner scope is still open. Other threads are not affected and use sessions of their own. Ending the scope always releases the thread, even when the rollback fails.

      Callbacks registered with afterCommit(Runnable) inside the joined transaction do not run when it is rolled back.

      Returns:
      the open scope, never null; the caller must close it
      Throws:
      UnsupportedOperationException - if this connection is not a root connection, such as a connection inside a transaction, a session or a pretend callback
      IllegalStateException - if the calling thread already has a joined transaction open on this connection, or is inside a transaction callback of it in strict mode
      QueryException - if the database refuses to start the transaction
      Implementation Requirements:
      The default always throws; only the root connection of a builder supports joining.

    • session

      default <T> T session(TransactionCallback<T> callback)
      Runs a callback on a connection held to one physical database connection.

      Every statement and transaction the callback runs on the connection it is given uses the same physical connection, so a session setting such as SQLite's PRAGMA foreign_keys stays in force for all of it, even when this connection borrows from a pool. No transaction is started; start one inside with transaction(TransactionCallback).

      When the callback throws, the session is discarded rather than closed (DriverSession.discard), so a pool that the driver can tell drops the connection, and a setting the callback could not restore does not reach the next user. A callback must not leave a transaction open through raw SQL; use transaction(TransactionCallback).

      Type Parameters:
      T - the type of the result
      Parameters:
      callback - the work to run, never null
      Returns:
      the result of the callback, may be null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if callback is null
      QueryException - if no physical connection can be opened
      RuntimeException - any failure of the callback
      Implementation Requirements:
      The default runs the callback on this connection, which suits a connection already held to one physical connection, such as one inside a transaction or in pretend mode.

    • pretend

      List<LoggedQuery> pretend(PretendCallback callback)
      Runs a callback on a connection that records each statement instead of running it.

      Reads return no rows, row counts are 0, and statement, insert and unprepared return true. No session is opened.

      Parameters:
      callback - the work to record, never null
      Returns:

      Throws:

      RuntimeException - any failure of the callback

    • withStatementLockWait

      default <T> T withStatementLockWait(long millis, Supplier<T> statement)
      Runs a statement with a limit on its wait for locks, as the timeout of lock(strength, Duration) does. The limit applies to that statement only: once the statement returned, the wait the transaction had before is back. If the statement throws, the previous wait is not restored, because the database may have aborted the transaction; ending the transaction takes the limit back. Query builders call it around a timed locking select.
      Type Parameters:
      T - the type the statement returns
      Parameters:
      millis - the longest wait in milliseconds, more than zero
      statement - the statement to run under the limit, never null
      Returns:
      what statement returned
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if no transaction is open
      UnsupportedOperationException - if the driver cannot limit the wait for a lock
      DriverException - if the limit cannot be applied or put back
      Implementation Requirements:
      The default throws IllegalStateException, because a connection outside a transaction has no statement the limit could stay with. A transaction connection forwards to its driver session and a pretend connection runs the statement without a limit.

    • transactionLevel

      int transactionLevel()
      Returns the depth of the transaction this connection runs in.
      Returns:
      0 on the root connection, otherwise the current nesting depth

    • events

      ConnectionEvents events()
      Returns the registry of listeners, the query log and the slow-query handlers of this connection.

      Every connection derived from one root, such as a session, a transaction callback connection or a transaction scope, shares the same registry, so a listener added on the root sees the statements and transactions of all of them.

      Returns:
      the shared registry, never null

    • afterCommit

      void afterCommit(Runnable callback)
      Runs a callback once the current transaction has committed.

      Outside a transaction there is nothing to wait for, so the callback runs at once on the calling thread. Inside a transaction it runs in registration order after the outermost transaction has committed and finished, which means the transaction's connection is already closed: the callback must use the root connection, not the connection it was registered on. A callback registered inside a nested transaction that rolls back is dropped. A callback that throws never causes a rollback; the first failure is rethrown to the caller of the outermost transaction with later ones attached as suppressed failures.

      Inside a transaction that the caller opened outside this library the outermost level is only a savepoint, so the library cannot know when the caller commits and registration is refused.

      Parameters:
      callback - the work to run after the commit, never null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if callback is null
      IllegalStateException - if this connection runs inside a transaction opened outside this library, or its transaction or scope already ended
      RuntimeException - any failure of the callback when it runs at once outside a transaction

    • canDeferUntilCommit

      default boolean canDeferUntilCommit()
      Tells whether afterCommit(Runnable) can wait for a commit on this connection.

      A caller of a model event or a similar feature asks before it writes, so it can refuse the write instead of failing after the rows are already changed. Inside a transaction the caller opened outside this library the commit is not known, so a callback cannot wait for it.

      Returns:
      true when afterCommit accepts a callback on this connection now, false when it refuses it because the surrounding transaction belongs to the caller
      Implementation Requirements:
      The default returns true. An implementation whose afterCommit refuses registration for a reason that does not depend on the callback must return false.

    • afterRollback

      void afterRollback(Runnable callback)
      Runs a callback once the current transaction has rolled back.

      Outside a transaction there is nothing to roll back, so the callback is dropped and never runs. Inside a transaction it runs in registration order after the outermost transaction has finished, under the same rules as for afterCommit(Runnable), whether its own savepoint or the whole transaction was rolled back. It also runs when the commit itself fails or when the rollback command fails; it is dropped when the outermost transaction commits and its own savepoint was not rolled back.

      When a transaction is retried, the callbacks of each failed attempt run once, in order, when the whole transaction call ends, on the root connection and on a session connection alike.

      The callback may run even though the commit landed: when the connection dropped during the COMMIT, its outcome is unknown and the library reports a failed commit. Undo logic must check the database before it compensates, for example before it refunds an order. A callback that throws never changes the transaction's outcome; the first failure is attached to the failure that caused the rollback as a suppressed failure, or rethrown when the transaction itself succeeded.

      Parameters:
      callback - the work to run after the rollback, never null
      Throws:
      NullPointerException - if callback is null
      IllegalStateException - if this connection's transaction or scope already ended

    • getName

      String getName()
      Returns the name the connection was built with.
      Returns:
      the name, never null

    • getTablePrefix

      String getTablePrefix()
      Returns the prefix added to table names.
      Returns:
      the prefix, never null, empty when none was configured

    • getDriverInfo

      DriverInfo getDriverInfo()
      Describes the database behind this connection.

      In pretend mode this still describes the real database, so code that picks SQL by database can record the statements it would run. A driver may borrow one database connection the first time it is asked, so with a pool of one connection, call it first outside a transaction.

      Returns:
      the driver's description, never null
      Throws:
      QueryException - if the driver has to ask the database and that fails
